findings.description: AWS access key and secret access key are hardcoded in plaintext within the instance user_data script, which is visible to anyone with EC2 describe-instance-attribute permissions and stored unencrypted in instance metadata, risking credential leakage.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true, leaving data at rest unencrypted and exposed if the underlying disk is compromised or snapshotted.
The snapshot is created from an unencrypted volume and has no encryption configured, meaning the snapshot data is stored unencrypted and could be shared/exposed without protection.
The security group allows inbound SSH (port 22) from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing the instance's management port to the entire internet and enabling brute-force or unauthorized access attempts.
The security group allows inbound HTTP (port 80) from 0.0.0.0/0 with unrestricted egress to 0.0.0.0/0, broadening the attack surface beyond least privilege network access controls.
map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, causing instances launched in this subnet to automatically receive public IP addresses, increasing exposure to direct internet access.
map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, causing instances launched in this subnet to automatically receive public IP addresses, increasing exposure to direct internet access.

findings.issue_category: missing encryption and public access controls
findings.description: The S3 bucket storing VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration, no bucket policy restricting access, and no public access block, risking unauthorized access to sensitive network traffic logs.
